extracted.intended_audience: federal credit unions (FICUs), credit union staff, trustees, attorneys, accountholders, and other stakeholders affected by NCUA share insurance rules
extracted.subtask_description: Final NCUA rule amending Part 745 to (1) merge revocable and irrevocable trust categories into a single 'trust accounts' category, (2) adopt a single streamlined coverage calculation, and (3) remove or revise other trust-account-specific valuation and procedural provisions. The page explains the rule text, rationale, examples, and implementation timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merger of revocable and irrevocable trust categories
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule merges revocable trust funds and irrevocable trust funds into a single 'trust accounts' category under §745.4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: funds held by trustees for beneficiaries are substantively similar regardless of revocability, so coverage should align with substance rather than legal form. This change will simplify determinations and reduce confusion. It does not affect the operation or applicability of state trust law. The rule defines included funds as: (1) informal revocable trust funds (payable-on-death, in-trust-for, Totten trusts), (2) formal revocable trust funds (written revocable trust agreements), and (3) irrevocable trust funds (established by written agreement or statute). Eliminates §745.4(h)–(i) provisions that allowed some irrevocable trusts to continue to be insured under revocable rules after a grantor's death.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streamlined coverage calculation (SMSIA × beneficiaries up to five)
rubrics_metrics.description: A single calculation applies to all trust funds: a grantor's trust funds are insured up to the SMSIA (currently $250,000) multiplied by the number of eligible beneficiaries, not to exceed five beneficiaries (effectively capping per-grantor coverage at $1,250,000 per FICU).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NCUA will presume equal treatment of beneficiaries for share insurance purposes (specific allocation among beneficiaries is irrelevant). Only beneficiaries expected to receive funds held as member accounts at the FICU are considered (non-deposit assets are excluded). The calculation mirrors the existing, well-understood method used for revocable trusts with five or fewer beneficiaries and is intended to speed determinations and payments. Examples provided illustrate application (e.g., POD with three beneficiaries insured for 3 × $250,000 = $750,000).

rubrics_metrics.name: Per-grantor, per-FICU aggregation limit ($1,250,000)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule imposes a per-grantor limit on trust-account coverage at each FICU: up to $1,250,000 per grantor (SMSIA × up to five beneficiaries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This cap replaces the separate treatment of revocable and irrevocable trust categories and balances simplification, timely insurance payment, liquidation facilitation, FCU Act consistency, and risk limitation to the Share Insurance Fund. The NCUA expects limited impact on accountholders based on historical balances; commenters did not indicate substantial effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregation of informal, formal, and irrevocable trusts for same grantor
rubrics_metrics.description: All informal revocable, formal revocable, and irrevocable trust accounts held for the same grantor at the same FICU will be aggregated when applying the per-grantor insurance limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregation means beneficiaries across all such accounts are counted together to determine the grantor's insurance limit. Trust-account coverage remains separate from coverage provided under other rights and capacities at the same FICU. The rule notes some accountholders who previously had separate coverage across categories may see reduced aggregate coverage after aggregation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible beneficiaries definition (who counts)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule adopts a single definition of eligible beneficiaries consistent with current revocable trust rules: eligible beneficiaries include natural persons, charitable organizations, and non-profit entities recognized under the Internal Revenue Code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule excludes contingent beneficiaries (those who take only if one or more named beneficiaries are deceased) from the share insurance calculation, codifying existing practice to include only primary, unique beneficiaries. It also codifies the interpretation that when an informal revocable trust designates the depositor's formal trust as beneficiary, the account will be treated as if titled in the name of that formal trust (and similarly if an irrevocable trust is named as beneficiary of an informal revocable trust).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of retained interests and ineligible beneficiaries from insurance calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantors' retained interests in irrevocable trusts and interests of beneficiaries who do not satisfy the definition of 'eligible beneficiary' will not be included in the share insurance calculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This removes prior provisions that required aggregating and valuing such interests (which sometimes required detailed review/actuarial valuation). The change does not prevent grantors from creating such interests under state law; it only excludes them from the insurance computation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of future trusts named as beneficiaries
rubrics_metrics.description: If a trust agreement provides that funds will pass into one or more future trusts upon the grantor's death, the future trust(s) are not treated as beneficiaries for purposes of share insurance; the natural persons or organizations who ultimately receive the funds are treated as the beneficiaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mirrors existing NCUA interpretations and avoids treating intermediate future-trust entities as eligible beneficiaries for coverage calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to name beneficiaries in account records for informal revocable trusts
rubrics_metrics.description: Beneficiaries of informal revocable trusts (e.g., payable-on-death accounts) must be expressly named in the FICU's account records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NCUA believes this requirement is not burdensome because informal revocable trusts inherently require the FICU to identify payees upon accountholder death.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of equal ownership for multiple grantors
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless the FICU's account records specify otherwise, funds held in a trust established by multiple grantors are presumed to be owned in equal shares.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This presumption is consistent with the current revocable trust rules and was retained in the final rule (replacing prior pro rata contribution language).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of accounts covered under other rules (exclusions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain trust funds covered by other sections of share insurance regulations are excluded from §745.4 'trust accounts' coverage—e.g., employee benefit plan accounts (covered by §745.9-2/§745.9) and trusts whose co-owners are the sole beneficiaries (treated as joint ownership under §745.8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board adopts these exclusions as proposed and is not changing current rules for these cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Six-month grace period for informal revocable trust co-owner death
rubrics_metrics.description: For informal revocable trusts, when a co-owner dies, the deceased owner's interest in the account continues to be insured for a six-month grace period; after that period, insurance is calculated as if the deceased co-owner did not exist and the surviving co-owner solely owns the funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This treatment is consistent with existing share insurance regulations and is reiterated in the final rule. Informal revocable trusts are unlikely to become irrevocable upon an owner/co-owner's death.

rubrics_metrics.name: Death of formal revocable trust owner does not reduce coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the merged trust category and the streamlined calculation, the death of a formal revocable trust owner will not result in a decrease in share insurance coverage for that trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because formal revocable and irrevocable trusts are insured under the same rules post-merger, coverage remains the same even after the six-month grace period following a grantor's death; the confusing prior rule that produced some irrevocable trusts insured under revocable rules is eliminated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of appendix to part 745 and updated notification options
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule removes the appendix to part 745 (which provided examples of share insurance coverage) and eliminates references to the appendix in headings and certain sections. Providing the appendix will no longer satisfy the notification requirement in §745.13.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FICUs will instead need to make available either the rules in part 745 or the NCUA's updated 'Your Insured Funds' brochure (NCUA to update brochure and online resources at mycreditunion.gov). The brochure is intended as a more consumer-friendly and easily updated avenue for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revisions to valuation and definitional provisions (§745.2(d) and §745.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Simplification of trust-account calculation permits removal of §745.2(d) (valuation of trust interests) and relocation/rewording of non-contingent interest and trust-interest definitions into §745.1; replaces deemed pro rata contribution language with a presumption of equal allocation in new §745.4(b)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The new definition of 'non-contingent interest' remains substantively the same but adds language to include present worth or life expectancy tables the IRS may adopt (e.g., similar to §20.2031-7). Many changes are non-substantive, intended to improve readability and conform to the streamlined trust-account calculation. Cross-references (e.g., in §745.9) are updated accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date and implementation timeline (Dec 1, 2026)
rubrics_metrics.description: The effective date for the trust-account changes is delayed until December 1, 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The delay (mirroring the FDIC timeline) provides FICUs, accountholders, and the NCUA time to prepare: FICUs can train staff and update publications; accountholders can review coverage and adjust accounts; NCUA must update its share insurance estimator and guidance publications. The Board discusses reasons for delayed effective date and not applying current rules to existing accounts elsewhere in the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples illustrating application of the final rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule includes multiple worked examples (payable-on-death, formal and informal revocable trusts, mixed ownership trusts, revocable plus irrevocable trusts, many beneficiaries) to show how aggregation and the single calculation apply and where coverage may be reduced relative to current rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples demonstrate: (1) POD with three beneficiaries insured for 3 × SMSIA = $750,000 and separate single ownership coverage for other accounts; (2) two grantors with three beneficiaries insured for 2 × 3 × SMSIA = $1,500,000; (3) aggregation across multiple trust accounts for same grantor; (4) revocable + irrevocable aggregation may reduce total coverage relative to prior separate-category treatment; (5) trusts naming more than five beneficiaries are capped at five for calculation (e.g., seven beneficiaries → 5 × $250,000 = $1,250,000). These examples are illustrative, not exhaustive.
